name: Apple fruit water
lead: Apple fruit water is a water-based extract of apple fruit used in cosmetics as a mild source of fruit acids and polyphenols. The sources reviewed contain a single dedicated study: a 2018 report on a cream containing 6 percent wild apple fruit water extract, said to contain 3.5 percent alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) along with polyphenolic compounds, stabilized with biodegradable alkyl-polyglucoside emulsifiers [1].

Alpha hydroxy acids are used in cosmetics for chemical exfoliation, with mild irritation, redness and flaking as the most common side effects, and the FDA has warned that they can increase the likelihood of sunburn [2]. Beyond this one cosmetic formulation paper, little published research on apple fruit water as a skincare ingredient was found.
infobox: AHAs (3.5% in the studied extract), polyphenols [1]

paras: The extract described in the 2018 study was a water extract of wild apple fruit, incorporated into an emulsion cream at 6 percent [1]. The authors characterized the cream for physical properties, antioxidant activity over 180 days of storage, and in-vivo skin effects [1].

AHAs, which include glycolic, lactic, mandelic and citric acid, are used for chemical exfoliation of the skin [2]. The FDA and the Cosmetic Ingredient Review panel consider AHAs safe at low concentrations, at pH above 3.5, with safety instructions, and the FDA has advised caution about sun exposure [2].

The one relevant paper is a cosmetic formulation study that combined in-vitro characterization with in-vivo testing of the apple extract cream for stability, safety, antioxidant activity and efficiency [1]. The sources reviewed give no further detail on its results, and no independent human trial of apple fruit water as a skincare ingredient was found. Registered trials that mention apples concern food or juice intake, such as glycemic response and cardiometabolic markers, and do not concern skin.

refs.title: Standardized extract of wild apple fruit in alkyl-polyglucoside-based cosmetic cream - estimation of stability, safety, antioxidant activity and efficiency

card.summary: A mild fruit-acid botanical water in some creams; one formulation study and little else.
card.aka: Malus fruit water, apple fruit extract
card.note: Very thin evidence base; AHA-containing products can raise sun sensitivity.

quick.overview:
Apple fruit water is a water extract of apple used in cosmetics as a gentle source of fruit acids and polyphenols.

The sources reviewed contain only one cosmetic formulation study, so little can be said about its effects on appearance.
quick.mechanism: The studied extract contained about 3.5 percent alpha hydroxy acids, which act as chemical exfoliants, plus antioxidant polyphenols.
quick.risks: AHAs commonly cause mild irritation, redness and flaking, and the FDA has warned they may increase sunburn likelihood.
